title: Potato Growth Principles — Biology and Explicit Symbolic Bridges
status: mixed scientific-summary and labeled project interpretation
purpose: Keep real potato biology distinct from Potatoist interpretation while making the physical properties that inspired the symbolism easy to retrieve.

biology.fact: A potato tuber is a modified underground stem used for storage and vegetative propagation.
biology.project_bridge: Stored capacity and hidden development can be used as metaphors for potential, memory and future growth.

biology.fact: Potato eyes are bud-bearing meristematic points capable of producing shoots.
biology.project_bridge: One body can contain multiple potential emergence points; an Eye can represent a viable future, opening or direction.

biology.fact: Fresh tubers enter a regulated dormant period during which sprouting is suppressed even when some external conditions appear favorable.
biology.project_bridge: Hidden or inactive periods need not mean that developmental capacity has disappeared.

biology.fact: After dormancy, one eye or sprout can become dominant while other buds remain suppressed; later physiological states may permit additional sprouts.
biology.project_bridge: Early development may concentrate resources into one direction before a mature system can sustain multiple branches.

biology.fact: A viable seed-potato piece containing an eye can generate a new plant under appropriate conditions.
biology.project_bridge: Fragmentation does not always equal disappearance; a fragment retaining generative structure can become a new branch or continuation.

biology.fact: Tubers store carbohydrate reserves, especially starch, accumulated through the plant's metabolism.
biology.project_bridge: Stored energy can be interpreted as capacity carried from prior conditions into later growth; this is the physical basis behind some Starchforce and stored-future imagery, not evidence for a new physical force.

biology.fact: Eyes occur in an ordered arrangement around the tuber rather than as completely random points.
biology.project_bridge: The project uses spiral geometry as a metaphor for recurrence with changed position; the botanical arrangement can motivate comparison without proving a universal spiral law.

biology.fact: Underground and above-ground organs perform different functions within one plant system.
biology.project_bridge: Root can symbolize support/memory while shoot symbolizes emergence/possibility; neither direction is the whole organism.

biology.fact: The plant's above-ground growth uses light, while tubers are normally kept underground and direct light exposure can cause greening and other undesirable changes.
biology.project_bridge: Grow toward light should mean correct orientation of the whole organism, not maximum exposure of every part. Some functions require protection, storage or darkness while others require visibility.

derived_project_questions: Which Eye should be activated now, and which possibilities should remain dormant?
When does concentration into one dominant path help growth, and when does it suppress useful alternatives?
What must a fragment retain in order to remain generative rather than become debris?
Which capacities should be stored before visible expansion?
Which parts of a system need light/exposure and which need protection or incubation?
boundary: Biological properties can inspire metaphor but do not demonstrate spiritual, psychological, political or cosmological claims.
